newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia, Singapore to discuss trade and defence.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia, Singapore to discuss trade and defence.

text.p: Australia and Singapore would discuss a strategy for promoting freer world trade during an inaugural meeting of senior ministers this week, Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Tuesday.

The meeting in Canberra would cover trade issues in the lead-up to November's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum and December's World Trade Organisation meeting, as well as a range of defence and bilateral issues, Downer said.
The inaugural Singapore-Australia joint ministerial committee, due to begin on Wednesday, would help strengthen the substantial bilateral relationship, Downer said in a statement.
"The convening of the committee reflects the deep shared interests and close relationship between Singapore and Australia," Downer said.
Singapore is one of Australia's closest allies in the Asia. Australia and Singapore are members of the Five Power Defence Arrangements pact, along with Malaysia, Britain and New Zealand.
The pair also share strong trade and defence links and are fellow members of the British Commonwealth. Bilateral trade was worth A$6.3 billion (US$5.0 billion) in the year to June 30, 1996.

Downer, Trade Minister Tim Fischer and Defence Minister Ian MacLachlan will meet Singapore Foreign Minister S. Jayakumar, Trade Minister Yeo Cheow Tong and Second Minister for Defence Teo Chee Hean in the two-day talks. (A$1 = US$0.79)
